correctness.rationale: For all odd primes p and n>=1: the binomial identity gives E=(C-A)/p. Lucas modulo p proves C=A (mod p), so E is integral; Lucas modulo 2 makes E parity exactly the binary superset condition. A separate exact identity, proved by fixing the coefficient of each binary bit e_h of j, equates Rowland’s printed floor-sum expression with the deposition sum of all free bits. The resulting bijection handles every original j and every exception residue. Boundary n<2p is covered. The package verifier reproduces 429 prime parameter sets and 11,816 exact binomial cases; these finite checks corroborate, not replace, the proof.

originality.rationale: The original full 2011 Rowland primary article explicitly states this exact floor-sum residue condition as unproved Conjecture 2. Its proven fractional-part congruence and standard Lucas parity supply the known arithmetic component; the complete digit-deposition identity proves the missing printed parameter equivalence. Targeted searches for resolution, equivalent binary mask forms, and broader binomial-mod-n coverage found no result already proving this equivalence. Global literature completeness is not claimed.
residual_risks: An equivalent proof of Rowland’s exact original conjecture could appear in unindexed literature or uninspected later publications.
The 2010 related paper was only compared at abstract level; a broader implication in another source cannot be absolutely excluded.
Bibliographic searches and absence of matching records do not establish absolute novelty.

value.rationale: This resolves an explicitly published conjecture with all positive indices and every odd prime, replacing a nonobvious, existential floor-sum index test with a single bitwise mask comparison. A complete bijection classifies the 2^(L-s_2(2p)) exceptional residues. This is a natural structural answer motivated by an existing problem, not a routine fixed numerical subcase.
